pk.context: 6 mg/kg intravenous, steady state, healthy adults

pill.desc: pale yellow to light brown lyophilized powder in a single-dose vial

tell: A cyclic lipopeptide from fermentation of Streptomyces roseosporus that depolarizes bacterial cell membranes.

clues.text: Protein binding is 90% to 93%. The kidneys excrete most of the dose, and metabolism is minimal.
Derived from fermentation of a Streptomyces species, with a molecular weight of 1620.67; supplied as a sterile, preservative-free lyophilized powder.
Approved under an NDA as 500 mg and 250 mg vials, dosed once every 24 hours.
No boxed warning; contraindicated with known hypersensitivity to it. Diarrhea and vomiting are the most common reactions in children.
Complicated skin and skin structure infections in adults and children, and Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections, but not pneumonia.
It binds bacterial cell membranes and causes rapid depolarization of membrane potential, which inhibits DNA, RNA and protein synthesis.
The generic name begins with D and has ten letters.
